check_text:
protocol.py: 2 biology problems (1 error, 1 note).

1. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: water (tube A2 in slot 3)
   line 33:  p20.transfer(50, tuberack['A2'], dest, new_tip='never')   # water
   At line 33 the tip went into water (tube A2 in slot 3) while it still carried bsa (tube
   A1 in slot 3) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of
   it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong
   there. Liquid drawn from it then took the unwanted material along into 1 other well: well
   A9 in slot 1.
   Affected: tube A2 in slot 3.
   Also reached 1 other well: well A9 in slot 1.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 33 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [e6d6139e6558]

2. NOTE CONTAM-WELL: A used tip carried water (tube A2 in slot 3) into well A1 in slot 1 it
was never meant for
   line 34:  p20.transfer(50, plate[std_wells[i-1]], dest, new_tip='never')  # BSA from previous well
   At line 34 the tip touched the liquid in well A1 in slot 1 while it still carried water
   (tube A2 in slot 3) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a
   little of it in the next liquid it touches. The protocol never transfers that liquid into
   this well on purpose, so it was not meant to be there. If the wells hold different
   samples, each now holds a little of another.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 1.
   Fix: Use a fresh tip for each well at line 34. If one tip must serve many wells, dispense
   from above the liquid (for example `well.top()`) so that the tip never touches what is
   already in the well.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   [7ab8bad4fe31]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
